name: tcrypt_header
description: Read a VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt volume header with cryptsetup's tcrypt mode, for a password (and, optionally, keyfiles) the case supplies. VeraCrypt and TrueCrypt leave no on-disk signature (crypto_id, identify/headers): this is the next reader once a candidate password exists. The password is read from `password_file` (a 0600 file; never a value on this tool's command line, in its environment, or in a file it writes) and given to `cryptsetup tcryptDump` on that program's own stdin. The answer says whether a header decrypted and, when it did, the header's non-secret fields from cryptsetup's own TCRYPT dump: version, driver requirement, flags, sector size, the master-key offset, the volume and hidden-volume sizes, the PBKDF and its hash, the cipher chain and mode, and the key size in bits; never the volume key, a salt, or any other derived secret. A header that does not decrypt is not proof the volume is not VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt: the password may be wrong, `header` may name the wrong region (normal, hidden or backup), or a keyfile may be missing. `pim` (VeraCrypt's Personal Iteration Multiplier) is refused, named: cryptsetup's --veracrypt-pim puts the number on its command line and --veracrypt-query-pim needs an interactive terminal, and whether a PIM may go on argv needs a decision this version does not have. `offset` is bytes, must be a multiple of 512 (cryptsetup's own --offset is in 512-byte sectors), and `source_kind: "device"` is required for a block device; a symbolic link, a FIFO or a socket named as `source` or a keyfile is refused. It refuses as JSON, before reading anything else (its own stdin included), when the call is not a job the harness ran as secret output (`SECRET_OUTPUT=1`); its manifest's `secret_output: "required"` makes every job of this tool one. It stops on SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP with one JSON answer and exit 128 + the signal, ending cryptsetup first; a read that has not returned after the tool's own clock and a grace period ends it with one partial answer (exit 0). A missing cryptsetup (macOS has none) answers `unavailable`, naming the program. A path shaped like a recovery password, an identifier or any other secret is withheld from every path this tool prints, by the shape rule its siblings carry.

source.description: The file or block device that may hold a VeraCrypt or TrueCrypt volume

source_kind.description: "file" (default) for a regular file, "device" for a block device; source must match, and a symbolic link is refused either way

password_file.description: A file holding the one candidate password this attempt tries (at most 4096 bytes; a trailing newline is dropped). Never a value given inline

keyfiles.description: Up to 16 keyfile paths, given to cryptsetup as --key-file; each must be a regular file, not a symbolic link

offset.description: Byte offset of the volume within source (default 0); must be a multiple of 512

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 60, 1 to 110; the manifest's timeout is 120)
